heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroData.subtitle: Hire rapidly in the DRC without local entity risks
heroData.description: Navigate the complex Congolese labor laws with a compliant Employer of Record solution.
heroData.bestFor: Mining projects, NGOs, and market testers

steps.title: Requirement Analysis
steps.description: Defining the scope, salary net-to-gross calculations, and mandatory benefits for Kinshasa or other provinces.

steps.title: KYC & Compliance
steps.description: Completing Know-Your-Customer (KYC) checks, crucial in the DRC for anti-money laundering compliance.

steps.title: Employment Contract
steps.description: Drafting a bilingual (French/English) contract compliant with the Congolese Labor Code (Code du Travail).

steps.title: Social Security Registration
steps.description: Registering the employee with CNSS (National Social Security Fund) and INPP (Vocational Training).

steps.title: Payroll Setup
steps.description: Establishing the payroll channel, often requiring USD to CDF conversion protocols or direct hard currency payments.

rows.label: Monthly Management Fee
values: Per employee per month. Higher due to complex local compliance.

rows.label: Setup / Onboarding Fee
values: One-time fee covering contract review and legal setup.

rows.label: Security Deposit
values: 1-2 Months Salary
Refundable deposit to cover severance and notice periods.

items.title: Currency Volatility
items.text: The Congolese Franc (CDF) fluctuates. Contracts often denominated in USD, but payments may require local currency conversion rules.

items.title: Provincial Nuances
items.text: Labor inspectors in Katanga (mining region) may have different enforcement priorities than in Kinshasa.

items.title: Severance Risks
items.text: Dismissing employees is difficult and costly. EORs will require strict adherence to disciplinary procedures.

items.title: Medical Checks
items.text: Pre-employment medical examinations are often mandatory and must be conducted by certified practitioners.

items.title: Visa d'Établissement de Travail
items.description: The standard long-term work visa. Requires a specific work contract endorsed by the ONEM (National Employment Office).

items.title: Carte de Travail
items.description: Work Permit card issued by the Ministry of Labor. Must be obtained before the Visa d'Établissement.

items.title: Visa Volant (Flying Visa)
items.description: A short-term authorization often used for specific missions or while waiting for the long-term visa. Not a substitute for a full work permit.

items.title: Residence Card
items.description: Once the work visa is secured, the expatriate must apply for a Residence Card from the DGM (Direction Générale de Migration).

faqs.question: Is it legal to use an EOR in DRC?
faqs.answer: Yes, but 'labor leasing' is strictly regulated. It is best used for short-to-medium term engagements or while setting up a local entity.

faqs.question: Can we pay employees in USD?
faqs.answer: The DRC economy is highly dollarized. Salaries can often be pegged/paid in USD, but tax reporting must be accurate in local equivalents.

faqs.question: How fast can we hire?
faqs.answer: Expect 2-4 weeks. Background checks and medical clearances can add delays compared to other regions.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle taxes?
faqs.answer: Yes, the EOR deducts IPH (Income Tax) and social contributions (CNSS, INPP, ONEM) and remits them to the authorities.

items.title: Standard Work Week
items.description: 45 hours per week (often 8 hours/day mon-fri, 5 hours sat).

items.title: Probation Period
items.description: Typically 1-6 months depending on the role classification.

items.title: Notice Period
items.description: 14 working days for <1 year service, increasing with tenure.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculate IPH (Impot Professionnel sur les Rémunérations) which is progressive, and deduct standard allowances.

steps.title: Social Security Declaration
steps.description: Prepare the CNSS (Pension/Risk) and INPP (Training) declarations. Unlike some countries, multiple agencies are involved.

steps.title: Currency Conversion
steps.description: If paying in USD, ensure the exchange rate used for tax reporting matches the official Central Bank rate on the transaction day.

steps.title: Net Salary Disbursement
steps.description: Transfer funds to employee accounts. Bank transfers are standard in urban centers (Kinshasa, Lubumbashi).

steps.title: Remittance to Authorities
steps.description: Pay withheld taxes to the DGI (Direction Générale des Impôts) and social contributions to CNSS/INPP/ONEM by the 15th of the following month.

rows.label: CNSS Pension
values: National Social Security Fund - Pension branch.

rows.label: CNSS Family Benefits
values: Family allowance branch contribution.

rows.label: CNSS Occupational Risks
values: Workplace injury and disease branch.

rows.label: INPP (Training)
values: National Institute for Professional Preparation. Can vary 1-3% but 3% is standard.

rows.label: ONEM (Employment)
values: National Employment Office (increased from 0.2%).

rows.label: CNSS Pension
values: Employee share of social security pension.

rows.label: IPH (Income Tax)
values: Progressive (0-40%)
Pay As You Earn (IER/IPH) tax on global income for residents.

rows.label: A.P.R.
values: Varies
Advance Tax Payment if applicable (less common for standard payroll).

items.title: IER vs IPR
items.text: Terminology varies (IPR - Impôt Professionnel sur les Rémunérations). Ensure distinct reporting from Corporate Tax.

items.title: 13th Month Pay
items.text: Not statutory but customary in many collective agreements (Gratification). Usually paid in December.

items.title: Expatriate Tax
items.text: Expat salaries are subject to IERE (Tax on Expatriate Remuneration). Verify the specific rate (often 25% or progressive).

faqs.question: What is the IERE?
faqs.answer: It is a specific tax on expatriate salaries, distinct from the standard IPR for locals.

faqs.question: When are payroll taxes due?
faqs.answer: Typically by the 15th of the following month. Late payments attract significant penalties (3-5% per month).

faqs.question: Is health insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: CNSS covers some risks, but private medical insurance is a highly expected benefit for professional roles.

rows.label: Training Tax (INPP)
values: 1% - 3% (varies by headcount)

rows.label: Income Tax (IPR)
values: Progressive (3% - 40%)

faqs.question: Are bonuses taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, almost all cash allowances and bonuses are subject to IPR and social contributions, except for specific non-taxable transport/housing allowances up to limits.

faqs.question: Is there a 13th month?
faqs.answer: It is customary but not legally mandatory unless specified in the CBA (Convention Collective).

faqs.question: What exchange rate should I use?
faqs.answer: For tax purposes, the official Central Bank (BCC) rate is used. For salary payments, contracts often specify a fixed rate or market rate.

items.title: Pay Slips
items.description: Mandatory in French. Must clearly show base pay, hours (if applicable), all deductions, and net pay.

items.title: IER (Impot Exceptionnel sur Remuneration)
items.description: A 25% tax on expatriate salaries, paid by the employer (not deducted from employee).

items.title: Payment Method
items.description: For amounts over $10,000 (rare for individual salary but relevant for payroll bulk), bank transfer is mandatory to prevent money laundering.

steps.title: Housing Allowance
steps.description: Ideally provided in kind or as a cash allowance limited to 30% of base salary to minimize tax exposure (check precise DGI limits).

steps.title: Transport
steps.description: Legal minimum daily transport allowance is mandatory for all employees.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroData.subtitle: Set up your SARL or Branch via the Guichet Unique
heroData.description: Streamlined entity registration through the GUCE one-stop shop system.

items.title: SARL (LLC)
items.text: Société à Responsabilité Limitée. Most common structure. No minimum capital requirement, but 'symbolic' capital is advised.

items.title: SA (Public Ltd)
items.text: Société Anonyme. Required for banking/insurance. Minimum capital approx $20,000 USD (subject to OHADA rules).

items.title: Succursale (Branch)
items.text: Can be registered for 2 years (renewable once). Good for temporary projects but creates a Permanent Establishment.

steps.title: Document Notarization
steps.description: Notarize the Articles of Association and Manager appointment letters. Costs vary by notary.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit share capital (if any) in a local bank account and obtain the certificate.

steps.title: GUCE Submission
steps.description: Submit a single dossier to the Guichet Unique de Création d'Entreprise. Covers RCCM, Tax ID (Numéro Impôt), and Id. Nat.

steps.title: Official Publication
steps.description: GUCE handles the publication in the Official Gazette (Journal Officiel) or a legal notice.

steps.title: Business License
steps.description: Obtain the 'Autorisation d'Ouverture' from the municipality/commune after incorporation.

rows.label: GUCE Filing Fee
values: Official consolidated fee for RCCM, Tax ID, etc.

rows.label: Notary Fees
values: Depends on capital amount and complexity.

rows.label: Legal Assistance
values: Professional fees for drafting compliant statutes (OHADA aligned).

items.title: Shareholders
items.description: Minimum 1 shareholder (SARL Unipersonnelle possible). Can be foreign.

items.title: Directors
items.description: Minimum 1 manager (Gérant). No residency requirement, but local presence helps with banking.

items.title: Address
items.description: Local registered office address Required (Domiciliation services available).

items.title: Criminal Record Check
items.description: Original 'Extrait de Casier Judiciaire' from the country of origin/residence (less than 3 months old) for all managers.

items.title: Passport Copies
items.description: Notarized copies of valid passports for all individual shareholders and appointed managers.

items.title: Proof of Address
items.description: Lease agreement (Contrat de Bail) or Title Deed for the registered office in DRC.

items.title: Specimen Signatures
items.description: Legalized specimen signatures of the appointed manager (Gérant) to be filed with the RCCM.

items.title: Capital Deposit Slip
items.description: Certificate from a local bank confirming the share capital has been deposited and blocked.

faqs.question: What is OHADA?
faqs.answer: DRC is a member of OHADA (Organization for the Harmonization of Business Law in Africa). Corporate laws are consistent with other member states (Ivory Coast, Senegal, etc.).

faqs.question: How long does it take?
faqs.answer: Theoretically 3 days via GUCE, but practically 1-2 weeks including bank setup and notarization.

faqs.question: Do I need a local partner?
faqs.answer: Generally no. 100% foreign ownership is allowed in most sectors (except mining/telecom which may have specific local content rules).

heroData.title: Staffing in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroData.subtitle: Recruit top talent in Kinshasa and Lubumbashi
heroData.description: Navigate the Congolese talent market with expert recruitment strategies.

steps.title: Market Mapping
steps.description: Identifying candidates in key hubs like Kinshasa (Admin/Gov) and Lubumbashi (Mining/Engineering).

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Leveraging local networks and platforms (LinkedIn is used, but local referrals and radio usage are common).

steps.title: Screening
steps.description: Validating qualifications (Diplomas) which is critical due to credential fraud risks.

steps.title: Interviews
steps.description: conducting interviews in French (Official language) and English (Growing business language).

steps.title: Offer Management
steps.description: Negotiating net salaries (often USD pegged) while contractually stating gross CDF amounts.

items.title: LinkedIn
items.description: Growing usage for white-collar roles, particularly in mining, banking, and telecommunications sectors.

items.title: Radio Ads
items.description: Radio Okapi and Top Congo FM are essential for reaching blue-collar workers and mass market candidates nationwide.

items.title: Alumni Networks
items.description: Universities like UPC (Université Protestante au Congo) and Unikin maintain strong alumni networks for junior talent sourcing.

items.title: Diaspora Networks
items.description: Crucial for finding 'Repats' (Congolese professionals returning from Belgium, France, or South Africa) for senior management roles.

rows.label: Junior / Entry Level
values: Standard placement fee.

rows.label: Mid-Level Management
values: Includes technical assessments.

rows.label: Executive / Senior
values: Retained search model often applies.

items.title: Language Skills
items.text: French is mandatory. English proficiency is a premium skill, fetching 20-30% higher salaries.

items.title: Expat Reliance
items.text: Technical roles (Mining engineers) are often filled by expats, but 'Local Content' laws are pushing for Congolese hiring.

items.title: Background Checks
items.text: Vital to check references physically. Digital footprints are often small.

faqs.question: Where can I find talent?
faqs.answer: Kinshasa is the talent hub for services/finance. Lubumbashi is the hub for engineering/mining.

faqs.question: What is the typical time-to-hire?
faqs.answer: 4-8 weeks. Notice periods in DRC can be long, but many candidates are immediately available.

faqs.question: Are fixed-term contracts allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes (CDD), but they are strictly regulated and can only be renewed once before becoming permanent (CDI).

items.title: Local Content
items.description: Certain sectors (subcontracting in mining) require majority Congolese staff/ownership.

items.title: Gender Equality
items.description: Labor code prohibits discrimination, but practical implementation varies.

items.title: Internships
items.description: A popular way to vet talent before full employment.

heroData.title: HRIS in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroData.subtitle: Modernize workforce management in DRC
heroData.description: Select HRIS platforms that handle SYSCOHADA reporting and multi-currency payroll.

items.title: OHADA Compliance
items.description: The system must support the chart of accounts and reporting standards mandated by OHADA.

items.title: Multi-Currency Support

items.title: French Interface
items.description: Essential for local HR administration team adoption and regulatory interactions.

items.title: Connectivity Tolerance
items.description: Offline-first capabilities are valuable due to intermittent internet in some DRC regions.

items.title: Global Platforms
items.text: Deel, Remote, and Oyster are gaining traction for EOR but may lack deep local payroll customization for direct entities.

items.title: Regional Leaders
items.text: Sage VIP and Odoo are widely used in Francophone Africa and offer robust localization.

items.title: Implementation Time
items.text: Allow extra time for training. Digital literacy varies across potential user bases.

rows.label: Local/Regional Software
values: SMEs using standardized packages.

rows.label: Global HRIS Suite
values: Multinationals requiring unified reporting.

rows.label: Enterprise ERP Module
values: $50+ / User
Large mining/telecom firms with complex integrations.

faqs.question: Can I use Excel for payroll in DRC?
faqs.answer: Many SMEs do, but it is risky given the complexity of progressive tax brackets and multiple social contributions.

faqs.question: Is cloud storage legal for employee data?
faqs.answer: Yes, but data privacy regulations (Digital Code) are emerging. Ensure the provider complies with general data protection principles.

faqs.question: Does the HRIS need to link to banks?
faqs.answer: Direct integration is rare with local banks; most processes involve generating a specially formatted payment file (txt/csv).

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Cleaning historical employee data, largely physical files or Excel sheets.

steps.title: Parallel Run
steps.description: Running the new HRIS alongside the legacy system for 1-2 payroll cycles to verify tax calculations.

steps.title: User Training
steps.description: Training local HR staff on the specific interface and reporting modules.

heroData.title: Accounting in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroData.subtitle: Ensure SYSCOHADA compliance
heroData.description: Navigate the OHADA accounting framework with local expert CPAs.

items.title: SYSCOHADA Revised
items.text: DRC strictly follows the OHADA accounting system (Système comptable OHADA). It differs from IFRS in presentation and chart of accounts.

items.title: Language Requirement
items.text: All accounting records and journals must be maintained in French.

items.title: Currency Limits
items.text: While bookkeeping can track multi-currency, statutory financial statements (États Financiers) must be presented in CDF.

steps.title: Fiscal Year End
steps.description: The fiscal year runs from January 1 to December 31. Closing entries must be booked by year-end.

steps.title: Audit Prep
steps.description: Drafting the financial statements (Bilan, Compte de Résultat, TAFIRE) for auditor review.

steps.title: Tax Return Filing
steps.description: Filing the Corporate Income Tax return (Impôt sur les Bénéfices et Profits - IBP) by April 30th.

steps.title: Statistical Return
steps.description: Submitting the DSF (Déclaration Statistique et Fiscale) to the Tax Authority.

steps.title: Approving Accounts
steps.description: Holding the Annual General Meeting (AGM) to approve accounts, typically by June 30th.

items.title: Société Anonyme (SA)
items.description: Must appoint at least one Statutory Auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) regardless of size.

items.title: SARL Thresholds
items.description: Required if meeting 2 of 3 criteria: Balance Sheet > 125m CFA equivalent, Revenue > 250m CFA eq, or > 50 employees.

items.title: Auditor Tenure
items.description: Auditors are typically appointed for a mandate of 3 fiscal years.

rows.label: Bookkeeping (Outsourced)
values: Depends on transaction volume and complexity.

rows.label: Annual Audit
values: Statutory audit fee for a standard SME entity.

rows.label: Tax Filing Assistance
values: Annual fee for preparing and filing the IBP return.

faqs.question: Can we use IFRS?
faqs.answer: For statutory purposes, no. SYSCOHADA is mandatory. IFRS can be used for internal group reporting only.

faqs.question: What happens if we file late?
faqs.answer: Penalties are severe, often involving a flat fee plus percentage of tax due, and potential audit triggers.

faqs.question: Is electronic filing available?
faqs.answer: The DGI (Tax Authority) is modernizing, and some large taxpayers (DGE) can file electronically, but physical stamping is often still required.

items.title: RCCM & Id. Nat
items.description: Ensure the Trade Register (RCCM) and National Identification numbers are active and updated annually.

items.title: Subcontracting (ARSP) Certificate
items.description: Mandatory for companies in subcontracting sectors to prove compliance with local ownership rules (if applicable).

items.title: Social Security Clearance
items.description: Obtain 'Attestation de Mise à Jour' from CNSS to prove no outstanding social debts.

items.title: Environmental Permit
items.description: Required for industrial activities, renewed periodically.

steps.title: Shareholder Register
steps.description: Maintain an up-to-date register of shares (Registre des parts sociales) at the registered office.

steps.title: Board Minutes
steps.description: Document all decisions of the Board/Management in the minute book (Registre des procès-verbaux).

steps.title: Annual Filing
steps.description: File the annual financial statements with the RCCM registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce).

items.title: Subcontracting Law (ARSP)
items.text: Strict rules now reserve subcontracting markets to majority-Congolese owned firms. Foreign firms must partner locally or face shutdown.

items.title: Anti-Corruption
items.text: DRC poses high corruption risks. Implement robust internal controls and FCPA/UK Bribery Act training for local staff.

items.title: Labor Inspections
items.text: Inspectors have broad powers. Ensure all personnel files (medical, contracts, pay slips) are essentially perfect on-site.

faqs.question: What is ARSP?
faqs.answer: The Regulatory Authority for Subcontracting in the Private Sector. They verify compliance with local content laws.

faqs.question: Can I hold board meetings remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, OHADA allows for video conferencing, but minutes must be physically signed and archived.

faqs.question: Do I need a resident director?
faqs.answer: Legally no, but for banking and daily administration (signing tax returns), a resident manager with power of attorney is necessary.

steps.title: Review Contracts
steps.description: Annual review of employment and service contracts to ensure they match current labor code interpretations.

steps.title: Tax Clearance
steps.description: Request a 'Quitus Fiscal' annually to ensure the DGI records match your payment records.

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax (IBP)
values: Standard rate on net profits.

rows.label: Minimum Tax
values: 1% of Turnover
Applies if 30% of profit is lower than 1% of revenue (or if loss-making).

rows.label: VAT (TVA)
values: Standard rate. 0% for exports and mining equipment (during exploration).

rows.label: Withholding Tax (WHT)
values: Standard rate on dividends, interests, royalties, and service fees paid to non-residents.

items.title: Depreciation
items.description: Standard straight-line depreciation is deductible. Rates are typically 5% for buildings, 10% for machinery, 20% for vehicles.

items.title: Head Office Fees
items.description: Management fees paid to a foreign HQ are deductible but capped (often at 10% of taxable profit) and subject to 14% VAT (reverse charge) + 20% WHT.

items.title: Start-up Costs
items.description: Can be amortized over a period of 2 to 5 years.

items.title: Interest
items.description: Interest on loans is deductible provided the rate does not exceed the Central Bank rate + 2 points.

steps.title: Monthly VAT Filing
steps.description: Due by the 15th of the following month. Must include detailed sales/purchase listings.

steps.title: IBP Installment 1
steps.description: First provisional payment (Acompte) due by August 1st (40% of previous year's tax).

steps.title: IBP Installment 2
steps.description: Second provisional payment due by December 1st (40% of previous year's tax).

steps.title: Annual Tax Return
steps.description: Final IBP return and settlement of balance due by April 30th of the following year.

items.title: Minimum Tax Trap
items.text: Even if you are in a startup loss phase, you must pay 1% of your turnover as minimum tax (minimum 2,500,000 CDF for large taxpayers).

items.title: Mining Code
items.text: Mining companies have a specific tax regime (preferential rates but strict ring-fencing).

items.title: Tax Audit Frequency
items.text: Tax audits (Contrôle Fiscal) are frequent and often result in significant reassessments. Maintain impeccable documentation.

faqs.question: Is there a tax treaty with the USA?
faqs.answer: No. DRC has very few Double Tax Treaties (DTTs). Rely on unilateral relief where applicable.

faqs.question: Can I offset VAT credits?
faqs.answer: Yes, VAT credits can be carried forward, but refunds are notoriously difficult and slow to obtain.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late filing?
faqs.answer: Penalties can range from 25% to 100% of the tax due, plus interest.

items.title: Cross-Border Payments
items.description: High volume of management fees or IP payments to foreign HQs attracts scrutiny on transfer pricing.

items.title: Consistent Losses
items.description: Reporting losses for >3 years will trigger an automatic comprehensive audit.

items.title: VAT Discrepancies
items.description: Mismatches between turnover declared for IBP and turnover declared for VAT.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Democratic Republic of the Congo
heroData.subtitle: Drafting robust contracts for DRC operations
heroData.description: Ensure your Master Service Agreements comply with OHADA and Congolese Code Obligations.

items.title: OHADA Uniform Acts
items.text: The cornerstone of business law. Covers general commercial law, companies, arbitration, and insolvency.

items.title: Language Mandatory
items.text: Contracts strictly enforced in courts must be in French. Bilingual versions are accepted, but French prevails.

items.title: Dispute Resolution
items.text: CCJA (Common Court of Justice and Arbitration) in Abidjan is the superior court for OHADA matters, offering a neutral venue outside DRC courts.

items.title: Force Majeure
items.description: Define carefully to include political instability or supply chain disruptions specific to the region.

items.title: Currency & Payments
items.description: Specify the currency of account vs payment. Address central bank repatriation rules.

items.title: Anti-Bribery
items.description: Include robust clauses referencing FCPA/UK Bribery Act and local penal code compliance.

steps.title: Due Diligence
steps.description: Verify the counterparty's legal existence via an RCCM search.

steps.title: Drafting
steps.description: Draft the agreement in French first, then translate. Ensure OHADA terminology is used.

steps.title: Legalisation
steps.description: For certain documents coming from abroad, notarization and MFA legalization (or Apostille if applicable) are required.

steps.title: Registration
steps.description: Register the contract with the tax authorities (Enregistrement) to give it a 'date certaine' and enforceability (usually 1-5% fee depending on type).

rows.label: Contract Review
values: Bi-lingual review by a local law firm.

rows.label: Retainer (Monthly)
values: For ongoing corporate secretarial and advisory.

rows.label: Hourly Rate (Partner)
values: Rate for senior counsel in Kinshasa.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Yes, under the emerging Digital Code, but for high-value transactions, wet ink is still strongly preferred by banks and authorities.

faqs.question: Does DRC recognize foreign judgments?
faqs.answer: It is difficult. It is better to use OHADA arbitration (CCJA) or a neutral seat like Paris/Geneva, though enforcement in DRC remains complex.

faqs.question: What is the registration fee?
faqs.answer: Contracts often need to be registered at the 'Enregistrement' office. Fees vary but can be a percentage of the contract value.

faqs.question: What payment gateways work?

items.description: Growing market of 'Kinois' influencers on Instagram and TikTok, mainly for lifestyle/fashion/music brands.

steps.description: Street teams (promoters) are highly effective for consumer goods.

faqs.question: What is the best way to reach youth?
faqs.answer: Concerts and music sponsorships. Music is central to Congolese culture.

faqs.question: Is TV advertising effective?
faqs.answer: Yes, but fragmented. National channels (RTNC) have reach, but private channels are popular in specific cities.

faqs.question: Can I target by region online?
faqs.answer: Yes, Facebook/Google capabilities exist, but geolocation can be imprecise. Target by city interest.
